data.title: Michael Saylor’s Strategy leads tokenized stock market with $491M – Details
data.description:
Michael Saylor’s Strategy never misses a chance to be in the spotlight, and this time, the company’s growing presence is seen in the tokenized stock market.

According to the latest update, four of CoinGecko’s top 10 tokenized stocks are linked to Strategy’s common stock, $MSTR, and preferred stock, $STRC.

Remarking on the same, Saylor said,

Digital Equity and Digital Credit are going global.

Strategy dominates tokenized stocks

As of the 8th of October, STRCx leads at $158.8 million, followed by MSTRx at $119.1 million, STRCon at $74.8 million, and MSTRb at $60.4 million. Together, these four tokens represent approximately $413.1 million, or 42.5% of the top 10’s combined market capitalization.

Meanwhile, other tokens include Circle’s CRCLB at $142.7 million, Circle’s CRCLon at $100.6 million, and SpaceX’s SPCXB at $83.9 million. At the same time, Strategy also reported leading the tokenized stock market by total on-chain value across all its issuers.

According to the chart, Strategy’s combined tokenized stock value is $491 million, comprising approximately $246 million in MSTR and $245 million in STRC. Circle follows with $338 million, while SpaceX has $174 million. NVIDIA, Tesla, Micron, Alphabet, SanDisk, Intel, and Securitize occupy the remaining positions.

Market conditions are tense

This comes as MSTR was trading at $151.47 after a drop of 1.24% in the past trading session. Meanwhile, STRC was trading at $99.45 after a drop of 0.020% during the same period.

If looked at carefully, Strategy’s Bitcoin [BTC] holdings have reached 848,000 BTC, worth $69.95 billion.

In fact, since adopting its Bitcoin treasury strategy, MSTR’s stock price has risen from $27.13 to $151.47.

Interestingly, AMBCrypto’s recent report also suggests that MSTR delivered annualized returns of 52% since August 2020, outperforming Bitcoin’s 38%, Nasdaq 100’s 19%, S&P 500’s 16%, and gold’s 12%, while U.S. bonds lost 0.91% annually.

Final Summary

  • STRCx, MSTRs, STRCon, and MSTRb lead CoinGecko’s top 10 tokenized stocks. 
  • Since adopting its Bitcoin treasury strategy, MSTR has climbed from $27.13 to $151.47.

data.title: Bitcoin’s price tests $80K – Why $402M BTC ETF outflows threaten ‘Uptober’
data.description:
On the 7th and 8th of October, the crypto long liquidations totaled a remarkable $1.707 billion. Since the market rally began in mid-August, bears have largely borne the brunt of liquidation events.

For example, there were $924.8 billion in short liquidations on the 21st of September, and $1.259 billion worth of short liquidations on the 21st of August.

The sudden turnaround was part of the Bitcoin [BTC] correction that was extending toward the $80k mark and could go lower.

The anticipated “Uptober” has gotten off to a rocky start. The spot ETF BTC flows in October were a negative $401.9 million already, as BTC faced a 1.93% drawdown for the month.

FOMC Minutes confirm tightening stance, deflating market sentiment

The minutes of the September 15-16 FOMC highlighted the reason behind the 25 bps interest rate hike last month. The primary reason was insufficient progress in lowering inflation.

Fed staff do not expect inflation to return to 2% by 2029, and have raised their inflation forecast for 2026-2028. New data confirming price pressure will strengthen the case for further rate hikes.

Crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. noted that after the Fed minutes were released, Bitcoin prices held at around $83.4k for a while before falling to $82.8k just 10 hours later.

The price decline began before the minutes were released, and the tightening stance the release confirmed likely reinforced the bearish view.

Notably, the Bitcoin Regime Score remained in negative territory. If the current reading of -22 falls below -30, the regime would shift in favor of sellers.

Bitcoin short sellers gain prevalence

The Bitcoin Funding Rate on Binance has fallen to -0.00215 as of writing, the lowest level since last January. This decline reflected the caution around Bitcoin price trends and the increased willingness to bet on continued selling, observed crypto analyst ArabChain on CryptoQuant.

Moreover, the Funding Rate was well below the 30-day Moving Average at +0.00458. This signals a marked change in derivatives market participant behavior.

There was evidence of whale accumulation and BTC outflow from exchanges, but the short-term bias remains bearish.

Final Summary

  • The Bitcoin price decline had already started when the Fed minutes were released, confirming the tightening stance.
  • The Bitcoin regime score needs to push above zero, and the price needs to reclaim $83.2k to signal a recovery.

data.title: $17B in crypto scams – Why Chainalysis and ACAMS are joining forces
data.description:
Crypto scams continue to rise, prompting ACAMS, a global organization that provides training and certifications for anti-financial crime professionals, to take steps to address the issue. 

The organization has partnered with blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis to improve crypto-related financial crime training.

Crypto anti-financial crime training takes center stage

Announced on the 8th of October, 2026, the partnership introduced an enhanced Certified Cryptoasset Anti-Financial Crime (CCAS) certification to help professionals identify, investigate, and manage risks involving cryptocurrencies. 

This was needed because, according to Chainalysis, illicit crypto addresses received at least $154 billion in 2025. Nearly $17 billion came from scams and fraud. 

In fact, at ACAMS’ The Assembly Las Vegas 2026, 79% of surveyed financial crime professionals identified crypto and digital assets as their biggest knowledge gap.

All of this happened at the same time when crypto adoption was expanding across traditional financial services. The latter was also the reason behind the increase in the need for anti-money laundering (AML), sanctions compliance, and fraud investigation expertise.

Remarking on the same, Jonathan Levin, Co-Founder and CEO of Chainalysis said, 

The advantage the transparency of blockchains provides only matters if practitioners have the data, skills and tools to use it.

Therefore, to bring a stop to this epidemic, the updated program includes revised blockchain training. Additionally, it also involves three new courses covering crypto financial crime risks, compliance programs, and real-world case studies.

North Korean hackers – the biggest hackers of all time

Yet, the picture is still dark, as North Korean hackers continue to deploy complex methods to launder stolen cryptocurrency.

And they are doing this by using specialist intermediaries, cross-chain transfers, token swaps, and over-the-counter (OTC) trading services. These networks help convert stolen assets into usable funds while making investigations more difficult.

For those unaware, North Korean hackers were responsible for the February 2025 Bybit hack, in which approximately $1.5 billion in crypto was stolen. Additionally, blockchain analytics firm zeroShadow, also confirmed that more than $1 billion in stolen funds was laundered between February and June 2025.

Then, in September 2026, attackers exploited Bitget, transferring an estimated $387.5 million in assets to wallets under their control. Elliptic linked the attack to North Korea, though investigators have yet to confirm the connection conclusively.

What’s more? 

Lastly, according to the Wu Blockchain analysis, attackers also moved funds across multiple wallets and blockchains, exchanged cryptocurrencies, and used mixing services to complicate transaction tracing.

This comes as the year 2026 has already lost $2.243 billion in total value hacked, as per DeFiLlama data.

Additionally, TRM Labs also reported that AI-enabled scam activity rose by roughly 500% over the past year. This reflects how tools such as deepfakes and voice cloning can help fraudsters scale deception.

Final Summary

  • At ACAMS’ The Assembly Las Vegas 2026, 79% of surveyed financial crime professionals identified crypto as their biggest training.
  • North Korean hackers have developed complex methods to launder stolen cryptocurrency, using specialist intermediaries, cross-chain transfers, and more.

data.title: Incoming lending wars? Lido unveils security-first protocol for $54B on-chain credit market
data.description:
Lido, an Ethereum-based staking giant, plans to expand into on-chain lending with an institutional and security-focused offering. In an X post, the team announced that the product, Lido Lend, will go live this quarter. As it stands, there are no specific timelines though. 

Lido Lend will be a modified version of decentralized lending platform Morpho Blue, but heavily skewed towards minimizing security risk and focused on professionals and institutions.

The project team noted that the move will be a ‘flywheel’ to its staking ecosystem. 

Lido Lend complements the stETH flywheel and Lido Earn. The synergy between these products opens a new growth vector for the Lido ecosystem, giving onchain natives everywhere a path to earn rewards in a user-forward and security-first manner.

Notably, the project singled out that it will only focus on well-known and liquid collateral such as stETH and WETH. This is likely part of the approach to reduce exposure to recent exploits tied to low liquid assets.

Can Lido challenge Aave and Morpho?

Well, Aave suffered immensely after the $292M KelpDAO exploit, with estimated bad loans climbing over $120M. Lazarus Group stole +89K unbacked rsETH tokens and used Aave to borrow liquid assets, including WETH. 

As a result, Aave adopted an aggressive framework to reduce such risk exposure, including axing assets with low adoption. However, it now seems that Lido sensed an opportunity from Aave’s security challenges. 

Analyst Konstantin Lomashuk echoed a similar view, claiming, 

Lido built the most secure staking solution in crypto: $24B+ staked. That market is solved. The next is lending. Too many hacks. Too much inefficiency. Lenders deserve far better protection. That’s what Lido Lend is built for.

Currently, the on-chain lending market is dominated by Aave, Morpho, and Spark (Sky, formerly MakerDAO). In terms of active loans, Aave dominates with 68% market share, followed by Spark at 13% and Morpho at 12%. 

Overall, on-chain lending’s total locked value (TVL) has recovered to $55B while active loans stand at $31B. Simply put, $55B in assets have been supplied, but only $31B has been borrowed, and Aave has been leading the market since 2021. 

Lido’s move will likely be read as a declaration of war in the lending market. However, the project denied the same and noted, 

Lido Lend is a tailored solution to meet the specialized needs of professional borrowers and long-term lenders, not the general purpose lending market. It is built to complement – not compete with- current market solutions.

Will LDO benefit?

It remains to be seen how the incumbents will readjust. That said, it’s unclear whether the growth will boost the LDO token or fuel its buyback program. 

At press time, the altcoin had pulled back 14% but was still within its H2 2026 rising channel. This suggested that it could rise higher.  

Final Summary

  • Lido to enter the on-chain lending market with a security-first Lido Lend for institutions in Q4. 
  • Aave currently holds 68% of the $55B lending market share.

data.title: Standard Chartered Singapore enters institutional crypto custody market – What’s next?
data.description:
Banking giants that were once critical of crypto are slowly turning towards the digital assets space.

On 8th October, Standard Chartered Bank Singapore announced its plan to offer crypto custody services to institutional clients and accredited investor corporate clients.

Standard Chartered’s crypto shift

For people new to the space, the bank will now securely hold and safeguard digital assets on behalf of these customers. This is very similar to traditional banks and custodians holding stocks, bonds, and other financial assets.

Here, the service will cover select cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, and tokenized real-world assets. However, the entire operation will be subject to Singapore’s regulatory requirements.

So, now instead of institutions having to rely entirely on crypto-native exchanges or specialist custodians to store their digital assets, they could potentially use a regulated global bank such as Standard Chartered.

This could make institutional investors more comfortable entering the crypto market because custody would come with established banking controls, security procedures, and regulatory oversight.

For those unaware, Standard Chartered already provides digital asset custody capabilities in markets such as the UAE, Luxembourg, and Hong Kong. Expanding to Singapore will further strengthen its global digital asset custody network.

What are the execs saying?

Remarking on the same, Patrick Lee, CEO for Standard Chartered Singapore, ASEAN & South Asia, said,

Singapore is an important centre for financial innovation, with a strong institutional ecosystem and growing demand for trusted digital asset solutions.

Echoing similar sentiments, Ole Matthiessen, Global Head, Transaction Services & Digital Assets at Standard Chartered, added,

As client demand continues to grow, we will continue investing in our digital assets capabilities across key financial centres, connecting clients to opportunities through a secure, integrated and globally connected platform.

This update coincided with a recent report by AMBCrypto. It noted that Standard Chartered is expanding its stablecoin strategy by becoming an authorized distributor of HKDAP, a Hong Kong dollar-backed stablecoin issued by Anchorpoint Financial.

Final Summary

  • Instead of institutions having to rely entirely on crypto-native exchanges to store digital assets, Standard Chartered will act as a regulated global bank.
  • Standard Chartered already provides digital asset custody capabilities in markets such as the UAE, Luxembourg, and Hong Kong.

data.title: Ledger investigates reported $80M crypto theft linked to CryptoBillis buyers
data.description:
Ledger is investigating reports that customers in Southeast Asia have lost their funds after they bought its hardware wallets through reseller CryptoBillis.

Blockchain analytics firm Arkham said more than $80 million was reportedly taken across Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tron. However, neither Ledger nor Arkham has confirmed how the losses occurred.

Ledger tells CryptoBillis to pause sales

Ledger said it had asked CryptoBillis to stop selling and shipping its devices while the investigation continues.

The warning focuses on customers who bought these wallets from the reseller in the past 90 days.

Anyone who has not configured a recently purchased device should avoid doing so for now. Customers already using one should consider moving their assets to a new Ledger device protected by a new recovery phrase.

That recovery phrase is the set of words granting access to a wallet. Creating a new one prevents anyone who may know the old phrase from accessing the replacement wallet.

Ledger also told customers to only contact it through official support channels.

The company did not identify the affected device models or confirm that any Ledger product had been altered.

Arkham tracks funds across 152 addresses

Arkham created a “ledger-drainer” label covering 152 addresses and published images showing how these funds moved across different blockchains.

At the time of this writing, the labelled wallets held about $71.6 million, including around $29.4 million in Ether, $17.68 million in Bitcoin, $13.65 million in USDD and $10.85 million in USDT.

The balance that can be seen is not the total suspected loss because funds may already have moved out of these tracked wallets. Also, changing crypto prices can change the dollar value.

Arkham says the theft is above $80 million, while some other investigators say the amount is reportedly more than $86 million.

The actual figure has not been confirmed by Ledger, so the current available figures remain estimates.

Also, there has been no actual confirmation of what caused the hack, and there is no confirmation of a company-wide Ledger exploit.

Final Summary

  • Ledger has paused CryptoBillis sales while investigating reports of customer losses.
  • More than $80 million was reportedly taken, but the amount and cause have not been confirmed.

data.title: Pyth crypto jumps 16% as DAO commits product income to PYTH buys
data.description:
Pyth Network [PYTH] has gained roughly 16% across two days after its DAO approved a new rule connecting product income with token purchases.

The policy creates a recurring source of demand for PYTH. But the amount purchased will depend on the money Pyth’s products generate.

Every dollar received will now buy PYTH

Under the newly approved “100% Rule,” all funds received by the Pyth DAO from its products will go toward accumulating PYTH.

Previously, the DAO committed one-third of its non-PYTH balance each month. Every transfer also required a separate community vote.

The new system provides standing authorization for future purchases, where stablecoins received by the DAO will be exchanged for PYTH on the open market and moved into its reserve.

According to the announcement, these purchases will still follow existing safeguards, and that includes a 5% slippage limit and a maximum of $25,000 per transaction. Pyth said each acquisition will be recorded onchain, and there will be monthly reports.

The first purchases under this new rule were made on September 30. Pyth’s reserve had about 42 million tokens when the announcement was made.

These changes come as its commercial operations expand, with its active annual recurring revenue reaching $11.49 million in September, rising 86% quarter over quarter.

Pyth crypto extends its rally

PYTH climbed 10.04% on Thursday [the last session] before adding another 5.70% at the time of this writing. It was near the $0.0857 price level at the time of this writing after briefly reaching $0.0878.

The continued rise suggests that buyers are still interested, even after the initial announcement. PYTH was also trading above its key price averages, showing that the recent upward trend remained intact.

But it was approaching the $0.088–$0.090 price area, and this is where sellers could begin to take profits. Its trend was also close to overheated levels, but it had not crossed that area.

If PYTH is able to go above the $0.090 price area, the rally could have more room. But if buyers lose control, the $0.080 price area looks like the first nearby support, followed by the recent trend level around $0.074.

The reserve purchases are not token burns. Tokens bought by the DAO will still exist and may be used to support contributors, builders, or other network activities.

Final Summary

  • PYTH gained about 16% across Thursday and Friday.
  • The DAO will direct the product income it receives toward open-market PYTH purchases.

data.title: Chainlink crypto slips 8% after CCIP 2.0 launch – Can LINK hold $12?
data.description:
The Chainlink [LINK] Cross-Chain Interoperability Program (CCIP) version 2.0 was released on the 28th of September. The groundwork for its Q4 cycle was laid, it was reported. Yet, the LINK price is down 8.12% from the $14.02 daily session open on the same day.

Moreover, the price drawdown was part of the wider crypto market sell-off. Chainlink crypto maintained its bullish overall trend, but investors were not extremely enthusiastic about the immediate bullish prospects.

Though the CCIP represented a sturdier bridge, the altcoin is also subject to macro conditions and LINK-specific sentiment shifts.

A call for a Chainlink crypto dump

A crypto analyst observed that Chainlink crypto was breaking below the neckline of a head-and-shoulders pattern it had formed on the 4-hour timeframe.

If LINK continued to trade below $13.56, the chances of a continued price move down toward $12.39 and $11.98 remained likely.

Towards the end of September, the chances of a Chainlink rally beyond $15 were good. However, the altcoin fell below a rising trendline support from mid-September, shifting its short-term bias bearishly.

On the daily timeframe, the swing structure was bullish. The $12 area was key, with multiple candlewicks to it over the past two weeks. It is possible that LINK would dip briefly below $12 to sweep the liquidation levels below before recovering.

The A/D indicator continued to show buyers were dominant. The Awesome Oscillator highlighted some short-term bearish momentum, but the indicator remained above zero to showcase overall bullishness.

Should Chainlink traders wait?

The 4-hour timeframe’s structure shifted bearishly when the $13.47 swing low (dotted cyan) was breached a few days ago. The technical indicators showed heightened sell pressure and downward momentum in October.

Notably, a deeper retracement toward the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement level at $11.72 was possible. Moreover, buyers can wait for a positive price reaction from $11.72-$12.0 before looking to buy.

Final Summary

  • The CCIP 2.0 upgrade introduced in late September fueled a price move to $15.77, but LINK has since retraced by 18.4%.
  • The higher-timeframe Chainlink crypto price bias was bullish, but the altcoin was affected by October’s market-wide correction.

data.title: Curve’s active loans jump to $76.18M – Here’s what it signals for CRV
data.description:
Curve DAO [CRV] has resumed its bullish push after its buyers successfully defended a key technical support level during the recent pullback.

The token has since then posted two consecutive days of gains, spiking by 10% over the last 24 hours after rebounding from the 20-day EMA around $0.36. Bullish sentiment remains intact, with buyers stepping in before the correction could deepen.

Beyond the price action, the recovery is also being reinforced by stronger network fundamentals. Could the positive fundamentals accelerate the current momentum?

On-chain activity continues to improve

Taking a closer look at the network’s on-chain data, several key protocol metrics have spiked alongside CRV’s price action.

To begin with, Curve’s total staked volume has maintained above $300 million across the past two consecutive days, pointing to reducing liquid token supply while reflecting growing long-term confidence among holders.

At the same time, active loans across the protocol have expanded to $76.18 million, signaling stronger borrowing demand and higher DeFi activity. Protocol revenue was also not left behind.

The network revenue has spiked to $158K, suggesting increased usage of the Curve ecosystem and healthier network fundamentals.

The combination of higher staking, expanding lending activity, and rising revenue points to improving ecosystem participation rather than a rally driven solely by speculation.

Can CRV extend the rally to  $0.4156?

The token’s long-term structure still leans to the bulls. On the daily chart, the token is still trading above major key EMAs, with the next big obstacle lying at the $0.4156 resistance level.

A break above this price will validate the continuation of the prevailing uptrend and may even spark some buying enthusiasm. However, buyers must first hold above the 20-day EMA, as it has once again established itself as a key support point.

If buying pressure remains strong and on-chain activity continues to improve, the probability of a continuation rally to the resistance zone is more likely to come into pass.

Final Summary

  • CRV has gained over 10% over the past 24 hours, extending its  recovery after finding support at a key EMA support.
  • The network’s rising staking activity, active loans, and protocol revenue point to its improving on-chain fundamentals.

data.title: Can NEAR crypto overtake Stellar again? THESE metrics suggest it could
data.description:
The most recent surge in NEAR Protocol [NEAR] is posing a threat to Stellar’s top-20 ranking. NEAR Protocol’s total value rose from $6.8 billion to nearly $7.2 billion as the token saw its value rise by about 7% in 24 hours thanks to increased buying interest.

Volume of transactions on NEAR was greater than $1.2 billion, which indicates new money coming into the market. However, Stellar [XLM] can’t seem to compete with the same drive, and therefore there is very little gap separating them at this point.

It’s worth noting that before this current trend, NEAR did overtake Stellar for a short period, but then Stellar took back its position.

Nevertheless, the difference between the two rankings is still small enough that it can easily go either way depending on whether there will be sustained interest in NEAR.

Robinhood expands NEAR’s cross-chain access

NEAR’s latest push is gaining a practical dimension as Robinhood Chain plugs into its cross-chain infrastructure. The integration enables users to switch out from one specific blockchain platform to over 180 digital assets available via 30 different blockchain platforms.

More importantly, this integration enables an intent-based approach to transfer digital assets.

For instance, when a user wishes to exchange Ethereum [ETH] for Global Dollar [USDG], they do not need to go through two blockchain bridges or access two separate platforms to achieve this. Thus, making it easier for users to access digital asset liquidity.

So why does this matter? Essentially, NEAR is turning something that has previously been a purely technical aspect of blockchain technology into a product available to the public.

With NEAR Intents already processing substantial cross-chain activity, Robinhood adds another potential source of flow.

Bitwise’s NEAR ETF gains institutional traction

This growing utility is now being reflected in regulated markets, where Bitwise’s NEAR ETF is attracting capital. In a post on X, Bitwise president Teddy Fusaro stated that NRR ranked among the top 10 by assets under management from 107 U.S. ETFs launched in September.

Despite the claims, there was no public data to substantiate nor contradict him.

The ETF was launched towards the end of September. As a result, there was little opportunity to accumulate shares prior to the initial trading day.

Yet assets reached about $65.4 million by the 6th of October, supported by $35.5 million in first-day inflows and another $13.2 million the next session.

This also indicates that demand rose quickly rather than increasing over time. More importantly, this placement provides NEAR with a significant amount of visibility to institutional investors.

If inflow continues, they will increase the degree of regulated exposure NRR has to NEAR, supporting NEAR crypto’s overall market presence by extending its network activity.

Final Summary

  • NEAR Protocol challenges Stellar’s ranking position as stronger buying lifts its market value.
  • NEAR needs sustained ETF inflows and network activity to extend its momentum
